transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29 16:00 UTC
Duration: 51 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Nora Li (Redwood CSM); Jordan Park (Helix Procurement), Maya Cohen (Helix Legal), Luis Ortega (Helix IT Security), Rita Sharma (Helix Eng)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, I think we've got about 50 minutes on the calendar, appreciate it. Quick round robin — if you can just say name and role.
[00:07] Jordan: Jordan Park, procurement, Helix. We're running intake for a vendor that will touch customer PII so legal and security joined.
[00:12] Maya: Maya Cohen, counsel. We'll be focusing on the DPA and MSA terms.
[00:16] Luis: Luis Ortega, IT security. I'll be looking at KMS, network, and logging.
[00:20] Rita: Rita Sharma, eng manager — leading the integration work.
[00:24] Alex: Great — Alex Moreno, AE at Redwood. With me is Priya Shah, our solutions engineer, and Nora Li from customer success.
[00:31] Priya: Hi all.
[00:33] Alex: Agenda — 1) commercial intake and contracting path, 2) security and technical constraints (KMS, VPC, retention), 3) hosting model and pricing options, 4) next steps. Any additions?
[00:42] Maya: Could you also confirm audit log retention and who has access? That's top of our list.
[00:46] Alex: Yep we'll cover that.

[00:50] --- Contracting & timeline ---
[00:50] [01:00] Jordan: Quick context — Helix needs vendor approval by mid-August ideally, procurement window closes the week of 2026-08-15. We evaluate cost, SOC2 status, DPA alignment, and any data residency requirements.
[01:14] Alex: Understood — that timeline aligns with a typical onboarding sprint. For contracts, we ship a standard MSA + DPA, and we can accept redlines; for enterprise accounts we often do a short SOW that scopes dedicated capacity or enterprise support.
[01:28] Jordan: On redlines — who owns the initial redline? You or us?
[01:31] Alex: We'll send our standard MSA and inline DPA first, then you can redline. Typical turnaround 3–5 business days per pass. We'll aim to have the first pass to you today or tomorrow.
[01:41] Jordan: Good. Pricing approvals: we need an itemized pricing sheet for hosted vs dedicated, including commitment tiers.
[01:48] Priya: We'll prepare a cost delta sheet — it will show per-token pricing, reserved capacity monthly fees, and expected unit economics at our recommended batch settings.

[01:56] --- Security & DPA questions ---
[02:00] [02:03] Maya: On the DPA, main asks — can we limit logging of customer prompts to a separate, opt-in retention bucket? Also, are logs sub-processors documented?
[02:12] Alex: Short answer: yes, we support configurable retention and can isolate logs. Our DPA lists sub-processors; we can provide an up-to-date list and a SOC2 report. We also offer private deployments which keep telemetry in customer VPC.
[02:27] Maya: For SOC2, is there a current attestation and date?
[02:30] Nora: We completed SOC2 Type II in November 2025; we will attach the certificate and the control map.
[02:36] [02:38] Luis: On KMS — does Redwood support customer-managed keys or only provider-managed keys? For Helix, we prefer CMK in our KMS.
[02:47] Priya: We support both. Hosted API uses provider-managed by default but we have a KMS integration path for enterprise where you can bring your own keys (BYOK) via customer KMS or HSM integrations. For Dedicated and Private, BYOK is standard.
[03:02] Luis: Network wise, can you support VPC peering or private link?
[03:05] Priya: For Private deployment yes; for Dedicated we support private connectivity options — VPC peering, private link, and firewall allow lists. We'll share a network diagram.

[03:12] --- SLA and operational questions ---
[03:13] [03:15] Rita: Our SRE is sensitive to P99 and tail latency. What's the SLA for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:20] Alex: Hosted offers a standard 99.9% uptime for the API endpoints; Dedicated comes with a stronger SLA package — 99.95% and committed latency targets depending on the GPU pool. We'll provide the SLA matrix in the SOW.
[03:33] Priya: Worth noting tail latency depends on batch policy and model variant; we'll include expected p50/p95/p99 numbers for your typical request profile once you share QPS and average sequence lengths.
[03:44] Rita: We do a mix — about 120 RPS peak for inference, average token length ~350, some bursts for end-of-day processing.
[03:53] Priya: That's helpful — for that footprint Dedicated is often a better unit-economics fit, but we'll show both options.

[03:58] --- Pricing & procurement nuance ---
[04:00] [04:01] Jordan: On pricing approvals, do you have an approval path for one-off usage credits or pilot pricing? We sometimes need a pilot rate for proofs of concept.
[04:08] Alex: Yes, we do pilot credits for initial evaluation — typically a 30–90 day pilot with a capped usage pool. For pilots that need to access sensitive data we often use private or dedicated pilot nodes.
[04:17] Jordan: And billing cadence? Monthly invoiced? Net 30 typical for us.
[04:21] Alex: We support monthly invoicing with Net 30 for enterprise; we can also do prepay credits for self-serve accounts.

[04:27] --- Legal deeper asks & carve-outs ---
[04:30] [04:31] Maya: A specific carve-out: we need assurance that customer PII will not be used to improve models or be visible to human reviewers. Can you add that to the DPA?
[04:39] Alex: We have a clause in our DPA that states we do not use customer content for training without opt-in. We'll flag that section and make it explicit. For human reviewers: if you opt-in to content review for safety, we'll indicate the controls; otherwise no human access.
[04:53] Maya: Also need clarity on breach notification timelines and sub-processor change notifications.
[04:58] Nora: Standard 72-hour notification for incidents, and 30 days' notice for sub-processor changes. We'll include that in the DPA.

[05:04] --- Technical follow-ups ---
[05:05] [05:08] Luis: For encryption at rest, what's the default algorithm and can we require AES-GCM?
[05:12] Priya: We use AES-256 GCM for encryption at rest; KMS-integrated keys use your provider's standards. We'll document the cipher suite.
[05:20] Luis: Can we run an initial integration test in a staging VPC with sample traffic?
[05:25] Priya: Absolutely — we'll propose a staging integration plan and a brief performance benchmark run. That'll be part of the SOW if we move forward.

[05:31] --- Objections & risk tradeoffs ---
[05:33] [05:35] Jordan: One internal stakeholder pushed back on vendor proliferation and asked if Helix could self-host everything. Why pick Redwood vs building in-house?
[05:44] Alex: Great question. Two quick points: time-to-market — we provide a production-grade runtime and orchestration which reduces months of infra work; second, cost predictability — our Dedicated plans let you buy reserved capacity and avoid hidden GPU ops costs. We can share case studies of customers who compared total cost of ownership vs self-host.
[05:58] Rita: Also, we don't want to take on the model ops and SRE burden right now, so leaning towards vendor service.
[06:03] Jordan: Noted.

[06:05] --- Recap & next steps ---
[06:06] [06:07] Alex: Quick recap — we'll send the standard MSA+DPA today, Priya will attach the cost delta and baseline benchmark numbers, Nora will include SOC2 artifacts, and we'll schedule a legal-only deep dive with Maya. Jordan will confirm procurement timeline and PO owner.
[06:20] Maya: For the legal deep-dive, please send the redlineable documents with track changes so we can iterate.
[06:24] Alex: Will do. Any final questions?
[06:27] Luis: One last ask — include a short appendix describing how KV-cache and prefix caching are handled; we want to ensure no inadvertent retention of PII in caches.
[06:36] Priya: Good point — we'll add cache TTLs and eviction policy notes to the SOW appendix.
[06:42] Jordan: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:44] Alex: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the package and meeting invite for the legal deep-dive.
[06:49] Maya: Thanks.
[06:50] (call ends)
